To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) resistance to Fusarium wilt in cotton is conferred by multiple resistance genes, (ii) the resistance genes are distributed throughout the cotton genome, and (iii) the cotton genome contains many disease-resistance genes that are likely to be involved in Fusarium wilt resistance.

the inheritance of race 1 resistance to FOV in cotton is governed by a single gene, and that QTL mapping and marker-sequence composition revealed the distribution, structure, and organization of disease response genes in the cotton genome.
the resistance gene model for Fusarium wilt in cotton is not simple and that the resistance is conferred by multiple genes on several chromosomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of molecular tools and strategies for the improvement of resistance to Fusarium wilt in cotton.
the identification and characterization of genes involved in the cotton response to FOV, with the aim of providing new knowledge for the improvement of cotton resistance to FOV.
the genetic basis of FOV race 4 resistance, and the molecular markers and candidate genes for race 1 resistance that can be used to improve resistance breeding in cotton.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
resistance to FOV race 2 is governed by single genes, while resistance to FOV races 1 and 3 is controlled by several genes.
the inheritance of FOV race 0 and race 1 resistance is complex, and that the resistance is governed by multiple genes, with the Fov1-C06 and Fov1-16 QTL loci playing a major role.
the inheritance of FOV resistance is complex and is governed by multiple R genes on nine chromosomes, with a major role for the C16 locus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
resistance to race 1 Fusarium wilt is a complex trait in cotton, involving multiple genes, and that the Fov1-C06 and Fov1-16 loci are major contributors to the resistance response.

the Fov1-C06 and Fov1-16 QTL loci are associated with the resistance gene(s) to FOV race 2 in G. barbadense, and the resistance gene(s), Fov1-1, Fov1-2 and Fov1-D, were mapped to the G. hirsutumspecific C11 and C08 chromosomes.
the Fov1-C06 locus is a major gene for resistance to Fusarium wilt in cotton.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the inheritance and genetic mapping of resistance genes in the cotton genome can be complex, and the genetic basis of resistance to a single pathogen race can involve multiple R genes, which can be identified using a combination of genetic, QTL, and sequence-based approaches.
cotton cultivars have multiple genes that contribute to race 1 resistance, which may be used to develop new cotton cultivars with broad resistance to Fusarium wilt.
the cotton genome harbors multiple R genes and that these R genes may be organized in clusters, as observed in the Fov1-C06 QTL locus.
